intuition: Store words as paths of letters, sharing the beginning of words with the same prefix. A search follows one letter at a time. Reaching a path proves that a prefix exists, but it does not prove that a whole word was inserted. Mark word endings separately.

Inserting apple creates a path a→p→p→l→e. That also creates a reachable path for app, but app is not necessarily an inserted word. Mark complete word endpoints separately with a key that cannot be a lowercase letter. Inserting app later adds that marker at the already-existing third-character node without duplicating its prefix.

Both search and startsWith follow their query characters and reject immediately if an edge is absent. Whole-word search additionally requires an endpoint marker. Prefix search does not: reaching the node itself proves at least one inserted word has that prefix. This separation is the central trie invariant.
Repeated insertion simply sets an existing marker again, and operation cost depends on query length rather than the number of stored words.

All three methods advance iteratively through characters. A permitted word of length 2000 therefore needs no 2000-deep recursive call stack; insertion and queries keep only the current node plus the shared trie structure.

steps: Create an empty Trie, then insert apple by making its five-character path and marking its endpoint.
search(apple) follows the full path and finds the endpoint, returning true.
search(app) follows an existing path but finds no endpoint, returning false.
startsWith(app) needs only the path, so it returns true.
insert(app) reuses the first three nodes and adds a terminal marker there.
The final search(app) returns true because app is now a stored whole word.

keyDecision: Whole-word search requires an end marker. Prefix search requires only a complete path.

concept.question: Why is following a letter path different from finding a whole stored word?
intuition: Independent word storage repeats shared beginnings. But combining beginnings also creates a subtle distinction: a path can exist without its prefix having been inserted as a complete word.

Store letters as edges from a shared root. Words sharing a prefix reuse those edges. Mark complete-word endpoints separately. Prefix queries need only an existing path; whole-word queries also need its endpoint marker.
concept.observation: An existing path proves a prefix; only an end marker proves a whole inserted word.
approach: Insert each letter along a shared path and mark its endpoint.
For a prefix query, require the full path.
For a word query, require the path and its end marker.
concept.correctness: Every inserted word follows its exact sequence of letter edges and marks its final node. A query follows those same edges, so a missing edge rules out that prefix. At the final node, the marker records precisely whether that full word was inserted. Shared prefix edges preserve all longer words without implying extra shorter words.

complexity.explanation: Each operation follows at most one edge per letter, giving linear work in query or word length. Stored nodes grow with distinct prefix characters across all inserted words.

pitfalls: An existing path proves a prefix; only an end marker proves a whole inserted word.
The same path can answer both queries yes when it has an endpoint marker.
